data.budget: web reads only; no model API calls; read-only on product code
data.claim: Partly. ddflow supports the linear, gate-ordered, human-approved, review-looped, worktree-parallel family by configuration today (prompt chaining, explore-plan-code-commit, review bots, approvals, worktree-per-agent, DAG of items, blackboard via the event log, durable resume at gate level). It cannot express, by configuration, a NEW workflow shape: item kinds are a closed registry of six (ddflow/config_sections/_kinds.py KINDS; kind_pipelines_problem refuses any other name), pipelines are flat ordered lists chosen only by kind and a docs-only diff, and there is no conditional edge, bounded non-review loop, in-item fan-out and join, branch selection, stage-scoped write permission, stage cursor or workflow version pin. The needed mechanism is one small declarative stage graph over existing primitives (WG-model with WG-edges, WG-loop, WG-fanout, WG-checkpoint, WG-select); the earlier workflow profile (R-workflow-profile-2026-11-11, WFP-*) covers stage-gated delivery, a bounded return edge and a routing predicate, but not loops with exit predicates, fan-out and join, selection, or arbitrary user-defined shapes, so it must be generalised, with WFP-stage-return and WFP-route-predicate becoming instances.
data.falsifier: A user-layer configuration, with no code change, that defines a new kind with a loop (until a predicate, capped), a fan-out with a join and a human checkpoint choosing the next stage, and passes a static check; or a pattern in the catalogue marked NO or PARTIAL that is shown to be expressible today by the recipe column. Also falsified if the workflow profile design already expresses loop-with-exit and fan-out-with-join.

WORKFLOW AS DATA ASSESSMENT. Today a user can define by config: which gates exist (command or agent prompt, reviewer family, required), their order per kind, review rounds, approvals, schedules, rules. A user cannot define: a new kind, a branch, a loop with an exit predicate, a fan-out with a join, a selection among attempts, a stage-scoped permission, a typed handoff, or pin a version, and nothing can check a workflow definition statically. Generic mechanism: a workflow record (SE-workflow-template layers) holding nodes (each resolves to existing gates, approvals, child items or lanes) and edges with a predicate (one shared evaluator, WG-predicate); four structural constructs only: conditional edge with a fallback, loop with cap and exit and on_cap escalation, fan-out with a join policy (EX-join-policies) over child items, checkpoint whose answer picks the edge; plus per-node scope, budget and produces/requires; runtime state is only a folded event cursor (WG-cursor); safety by static check (WG-lint) and simulation (WG-sim). A plain gate list loads as a linear graph. Versus the earlier profile design: the profile covers named stages, entry predicates, pipelines, a review ladder, a bounded return edge and a routing predicate, so it generalises as: profile = a graph instance with a fixed shape. It lacks loop-with-exit, fan-out/join, selection, scope, artifacts, budgets and lint, so it must be generalised and WFP-stage-return, WFP-route-predicate and WP-gate-stages declared instances or degenerate cases (WG-decide).

COMMON LLM ANSWER SHAPE (own reasoning under five framings: feature, production bug, large migration, research-then-build, continuous maintenance). Skeleton: 1 intake and clarify (ask only blocking questions, restate acceptance) 2 research or reproduce (read code, search prior work; for a bug, reproduce first and write a failing test) 3 plan (small reviewable slices, risks, rollback) 4 human checkpoint on plan 5 decompose and parallelise independent slices 6 implement in isolation, test first 7 verify (tests, lint, types, security) 8 review by an independent reviewer with a bounded number of rounds 9 integrate (merge queue, rebase, resolve conflicts) 10 release or stage behind a flag with a watch window and a rollback path 11 retrospective and lesson capture. Always added: caps on loops, budgets, escalation to a human after N failures, a definition of done, idempotent resumable steps. Per framing: bug adds triage severity, a minimal fix and a regression test before the fix, hotfix lane; migration adds characterization tests, a campaign ledger of units, per-unit green, strangler or dual-run, a stop-the-line rule; research-then-build adds a pre-registered question, stop rules, a decision record, then a spec; maintenance adds a schedule, a backlog triage, dependency and flake sweeps, an auto-PR with a cap on open PRs. Step vocabulary LLMs reach for: clarify, plan, decompose, parallelise, implement, verify, review, integrate, release, retrospect, with loop, cap, escalate, checkpoint. Cross-family comparison was NOT done: ddflow has no free-form question facility (ddflow review is diff-only; reviewers test sends a fixed buggy diff), so no model API call was made.

WHERE AHEAD: event-sourced log as a blackboard with replay; per-item lease and worktree isolation with glob locking; independence rules for reviewers; refusing silence as a pass (UNAVAILABLE distinct); person-only approvals; bounded review rounds; budgeted briefs. WHERE BEHIND: no declarative workflow shapes, no loops or fan-out as data, no workflow evaluation, no versioning, no stage-level resume, no per-stage permissions, no selection among attempts, stage spans for tracing.

HAZARDS the design must respect: a loop must name its cap (runaway); a fan-out must name its join and cap (cost multiples and duplicate work); a judge must not be the author family and must swap order; an unavailable fact never routes as true; an agent never answers a checkpoint; interrupts re-run work so stage entry must be idempotent (LangGraph lesson).

data.question: Can ddflow express the full range of agentic workflow patterns (chain, route, parallel, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, loops, search, debate, handoff, human checkpoints, campaigns) with configuration only, and what minimal generic mechanism closes the gaps?

data.alternatives: Per-pattern features (rejected: duplicated models, no shared safety check); adopting an external graph runtime (rejected: breaks event-log source of truth and r-reuse-core).
data.consequences: One validator and one cursor; loops and fan-outs become checkable; costs a new phase P-workflow-graph and a migration of WFP-stage-return, FUS patterns and FL-fanout to instances.
data.context: The field converges on graph runtimes (state, nodes, conditional edges, fan-out, loops, interrupts) and ddflow's item kinds are a closed registry of six with flat pipelines, so every new pattern would otherwise be a new hard-coded feature.
data.decision: Express workflow shapes as one declarative graph (nodes resolving to existing gates, approvals, child items and lanes; conditional edges; bounded loops; fan-out with a join policy; checkpoints whose answer picks the edge) layered shipped < company < project < user under SE-workflow-template. WP-gate-stages and the workflow profile stages are instances or degenerate cases. A plain gate list loads as a linear graph with identical behaviour.
data.title: A generic workflow graph over existing primitives, not per-pattern features

data.alternatives: Runtime-only caps (rejected: defects found after cost is spent).
data.consequences: Some legitimate open-ended loops need an explicit large cap.
data.context: Runaway loops, compounding errors and over-delegation are the recurring failure modes in the research (multi-agent failure taxonomy, multi-agent research lessons).
data.decision: A graph with a cycle lacking a cap and an exit predicate, a fan-out lacking a join and a children cap, or a branch lacking a fallback edge is refused at definition time by ddflow workflow check. Caps escalate to a person (park with the exact next call), never retry silently. The worst-case run count is computed and compared to a knob.
data.title: Every workflow loop and fan-out is bounded and statically checked

data.alternatives: Free model opinion as the selector (rejected).
data.consequences: Fewer subjective picks; judge-only domains (prose) need the stricter swap policy.
data.context: Judge models show position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias; reward hacking is common and instructions alone barely reduce it.
data.decision: Selection policies default to first_green, smallest_diff_green or majority of gate verdicts. A judge policy runs both orders, excludes the author family, and a disagreement is a tie that parks. Losing attempts are closed and recorded, never merged.
data.title: Choosing among attempts or voters is by measured outcome; a model judge only with order-swap and never the author family

data.alternatives: A second expression language per feature (rejected: r-reuse-core).
data.consequences: WFP-route-predicate and SJ-when depend on the facade; one fuzz corpus.
data.context: Three evaluators are planned or exist (job when, routing, approvals policy).
data.decision: Edges, WFP-route-predicate, definition of ready and job conditions share the SJ-when grammar through one facade; an unavailable fact never evaluates true and takes the declared fallback.
data.title: One predicate language for edges, routes, readiness and job conditions

data.consequences: Some legitimate refactors that touch tests need a recorded widen.
data.context: Measured reward-hacking rates barely moved when the model was told not to cheat.
data.decision: A stage may declare a write scope (red: tests only; green: no test edits; review: read-only) enforced by the lease and pre-edit hook, widenable only by a person; evaluation assets stay outside an implementing stage's reach (AP-protect).
data.title: Anti-cheating is a structural stage scope, not an instruction

data.body: From R-agentic-workflows-2026-11-11 (operator request 2026-11-11). Generalises WP-gate-stages, the workflow profile stages (WFP-*) and the FUS patterns into data: a user defines a new workflow shape by configuration, and ddflow checks and simulates it. Governed by the PROPOSED decisions D-wg-graph-over-primitives, D-wg-bounded-and-checkable, D-wg-outcome-measured-selection, D-wg-one-predicate and D-wg-stage-scope-structural. Opt-in; a project that does not enable it behaves as today.
data.title: Workflow graph: one declarative stage graph over existing primitives (conditional edges, bounded loops, fan-out and join, checkpoints, selection, scope, budgets), checked, simulated, pinned and shipped as recipes
